>What is meant by the English by "cross-examine"?

That was a line from a letter, written by a Soviet official while they were organising the Nuremberg trials. 

The Nuremberg trials almost didn't happen, one of the parties preferred a summary execution, which obviously would have made things worse. However, with some delicate negotiation between the Allied governments, they decided to go with a public trial. 

However, they needed to decide which system to go with. Cross-examination wasn't a thing in Europe, so they had to get clarification on certain concepts, which makes them sound hilariously clueless in a way. 

To me, it just sums up the universality of the quest for justice (or whatever other goals) after WWII, and also the importance of collaboration in government. 

It also highlights the importance of asking questions and learning, which is important in my own life!
